hi Caleb, Can you tell me what an HOA estoppal fee is
ChatGPT said:

Hi Nick — an HOA estoppel fee is a charge issued by a homeowners association (HOA) or its management company to prepare a legal document known as an estoppel certificate (or estoppel letter). This document is typically required during the sale or refinancing of a home that's part of an HOA.

The estoppel certificate includes key financial information about the property, such as:

  • Outstanding dues or delinquent payments

  • Upcoming fees or special assessments

  • HOA rules and regulations relevant to the property

  • Confirmation that the seller is current on obligations

The fee covers the administrative work to compile and certify this information. In most states, the fee is regulated, but it can range anywhere from $100 to $500 or more, depending on state law and the HOA’s policies.

Would you like to know who typically pays the estoppel fee — the buyer or seller — or how to avoid overpaying for one?
